Thanks Emily — this is great context. Below I laid out the simple, reproducible pricing math we reference internally so you can see the sensitivity to hit rates and prefix size. I'll include the scenarios in the quote too.

Assumptions (for the quick model):
- Base unit price (Redwood hosted reference) = $20 per 1M tokens (input + output). This is a notional baseline — Dedicated/committed pricing will be lower.
- Token composition: we assume ~40% of tokens per session are "prefix/system" tokens (system prompt + product descriptors), and ~60% are dynamic user/assistant tokens.
- Prefix cache hit rate = % of requests where the prefix is served from cache and does NOT hit the model. Hit rate only applies to the prefix portion.

Formula (simplified): effective_model_tokens = dynamic_tokens + prefix_tokens * (1 - hit_rate)
Effective $/1M tokens = base_price * (effective_model_tokens / total_tokens)

Scenarios (using your 120M monthly tokens):
1) Low hit (20%): prefix portion = 40% of 120M = 48M tokens. Cache avoids 20% of that = 9.6M tokens saved. Model tokens = 120M - 9.6M = 110.4M -> effective cost factor = 110.4 / 120 = 0.92 -> effective $/1M = $20 * 0.92 = $18.40

2) Mid hit (50%): prefix saves 24M tokens. Model tokens = 96M -> factor = 0.80 -> effective $/1M = $16.00

3) High hit (70%): prefix saves 33.6M tokens. Model tokens = 86.4M -> factor = 0.72 -> effective $/1M = $14.40

Notes and caveats:
- This is a conservative model: it assumes cache hits entirely avoid model compute for the prefix. In practice, very short prefixes or when prefix+context combined exceed certain optimized paths, savings can be slightly different.
- Catalog updates: if you update product descriptions, cached prefixes will be invalidated. For typical catalog churn we see 1–2% invalidation per day; that reduces long-term hit rates. We can model TTLs and invalidation patterns once you provide update frequency.
- Cold-starts and personalization: personalized prefixes (customer-specific) are less cacheable. You mentioned a lot of shared product descriptors — that plays well for caching.
- Unit economics: when we build the formal quote we'll show per-1M effective price at expected volume bands and include committed-discount tiers for Dedicated.

Next steps I recommend:
- Please share a weekly token distribution (even aggregate counts by day) and a short list of the top 10 most-common prefixes (we can sketch an estimated hit-rate distribution).
- I'll produce a one-page estimator that shows effective $/1M at Low/Mid/High hit rates and a committed-capacity option with reservation discounts.

If helpful, I can also run a quick POC on Redwood hosted with a small sample of traffic to measure real hit rates before you commit.

Thanks,
Aditya
